neighbours.label: names of ancient Egyptian (and other Bronze Age Near Eastern) kings and gods, and the frames around them ('tomb of', 'pharaoh'), as against the same frames with European royalty
fire: The museum holds a statue of Ramesses II carved from red granite.
Archaeologists found the burial chamber of Seti I in the Valley of the Kings.
A temple at Karnak was dedicated to Amun by the pharaoh Hatshepsut.
The priests offered bread and beer to Osiris and his son Horus.
Inscriptions at Abydos list the kings from Narmer to Seti.
Under Akhenaten, worship of the sun disk Aten replaced the old gods.
The Hittite king Suppiluliuma wrote to the widow of the pharaoh.
The mummy of Thutmose III was found in a hidden cache at Deir el-Bahari.
quiet: The museum holds a statue of Charlemagne carved from grey granite.
Archaeologists found the burial chamber of Edward I in Westminster Abbey.
A chapel at Windsor was dedicated to Saint George by the king Edward.
The monks offered bread and wine to the abbot and his guests.
Records at Canterbury list the kings from Alfred to Harold.
Under Elizabeth, worship in the old Latin rite was forbidden.
The Scottish king Robert wrote to the widow of the English lord.
The body of Richard III was found under a car park in Leicester.
